chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Hadeed from Jamil who said:

Muraazim asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was present with him, about the man who is present (travelling) and prays in his izaar (lower garment), wearing it as his upper garment. He said: 'He should place a handkerchief or a turban on his neck, which hangs down.'

key_terms.مُؤْتَزِر: Wearing the izaar as an upper garment (or wearing it in a way that exposes the upper body)

ai.seo_question: What should a traveler do if he prays wearing only his lower garment (izaar)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the practical jurisprudence of *satr al-awrah* (covering the nakedness) for travelers or those lacking full attire. It establishes that draping a handkerchief or turban over the neck is a valid, sufficient method to cover the upper chest and neck, reflecting the Shia emphasis on contextual ease (*rukhas*) in ritual purity and modesty.
